title: Quantitative proteomic analysis of oxaliplatin induced peripheral neurotoxicity
projectDescription: We performed a data independent acquisition (DIA) -based quantitative proteomics strategy to investigate the global proteome alteration in the dorsal root ganglion (DRG) tissues from mice injected with oxaliplatin for different periods.
sampleProcessingProtocol: DRG tissue samples were homogenized in lysis buffer consisting of 8 M urea, 75 mM sodium chloride, protease inhibitor cocktail, and 50 mM ammonium bicarbonate. Then, the homogenate was further processed with ultrasonication and centrifuged to remove the debris. protein concentration was determined by the BCA Protein Assay Kit (ThermoFisher Scientific, Waltham, MA, USA). Protein digestion was performed using the modified Filter Aided Sample Preparation procedure. Briefly, the lysates were reduced with 10 mM dithiothreitol (DTT) at room temperature for 50 min. The reduced proteins were alkylated with 40 Mm iodoacetamide for 40 min in darkness. The alkylation reaction was quenched by adding DTT to a concentration of 40 mM for 30 min. The lysate solution was exchanged to 50 Mm NH4HCO3 buffer by centrifugation with the 10 kDa centrifugal filter (Millipore, Burlington, MA, USA) before trypsin (Promega, Madison, WI, USA) was added at 1:30 trypsin-to-protein ratio (w/w) for incubation at 37°C overnight. The resulting peptides were collected by centrifugation and dried with a Savant SpeedVac concentrator (Thermo Fisher Scientific). The peptides were resuspended in 0.1% formic acid and quantified by Nanodrop (Thermo Fisher Scientific) before LC MS/MS analysis.
dataProcessingProtocol: DIA-NN (v1.7.12) was employed to perform label-free quantification. Swiss-Prot FASTA database for mouse (17042 sequence entries, released in January 2021) was downloaded from Uniport (https://www.uniprot.org/). The spectral library was established by searching five raw files of GPF-DIA against the FASTA database in DIA-NN. The output file “lib.tsv” was used as the spectral library. And then, the “report.tsv” files generated by DIA-NN was used for the downstream analysis. Protein expression matrix was generated for quantification using “Precursor.quantity” intensities by “diann” package in R framework (v4.1.0). Proteins identified with two or more unique peptides and three intensity values in at least one group were used for quantification. Next, the expression matrix was subjected to quantile normalization by R package “preprocessCore”. Missing values were imputed with the minimum value across the proteome data. The intensity values were log2-transformed for quantification and bioinformatic analysis.
